method.distance: great-circle metres from the entry point to the nearest vertex or point of the feature
method.bearing: degrees true from the entry point to that nearest point
method.note: Each number here is the shortest straight-line distance from the entry point to one charted feature, measured separately. They are not steps along one path, and swimming from one to the next is not the sum of them. The 2,000 metre box is the limit of what was looked at: nothing further away is reported, and an empty list means nothing of that kind is charted within it.
method.band_choice: The three chart scales are tried largest-scale first. A scale is used only when NOAA's own coverage layer says its chart covers this spot AND it has a coastline or depth area within 2,000 metres; the first that does both is what this record is measured from, and it is named on every record. A spot no chart covers gets a refusal, never a measurement off a neighbouring chart's edge.
method.depth_datum: Charted depths are metres below chart datum, which for United States waters is mean lower low water. They are not the depth at the moment you are reading this: add the predicted tide.
method.nearest_water: The nearest point on the edge of a charted depth area, with that area's own shallow and deep bounds (NOAA's DRVAL1 and DRVAL2). When `inside` is true the entry point is already within the depth area, the distance is zero, and the bearing points at that area's nearest edge rather than at the water.
method.contours: One row per distinct charted contour value within the box, at its nearest point, the six shallowest kept.
method.soundings: The five nearest charted soundings (NOAA's own Z value).
method.chart_source_date: The OLDEST of NOAA's own source dates (SORDAT) across the charted features this record is measured from — the coastline, the depth area, the contours. The oldest rather than the newest, because it is the one that cannot overstate how recently any of this was surveyed.
method.rounding: Distances and bearings are whole metres and whole degrees; depths keep one decimal. Coordinates are six decimals. NOAA's own depth values are carried through unchanged apart from that rounding.
